column1: # RDR-229 P3.5c (nexus-p2m1x.25): what P3.5c does with each Java reader of p35c-java-reader-census.tsv, one row per (kind, object, name_column).
# Hand-kept; tests/test_rdr229_p35c_java_reader_census.py fails while a census reader has no row, a row names no census reader, or a row breaks its rule.
# kind is always "java"; object is "<file under service/src/main/java/dev/nexus/service/> <table> <op>" (every line of that file, table and op share the row).
#   id             switched to read the id column (collection_id, physical_collection_id, ...) from gate 3 on the install; the name path stays until then
#   both           reads the id where the row carries one and the name where it does not (a reader of a table the stamp may not have reached); P4.1 removes the name arm. Needs a reason.
#   label-kept     keeps reading the registry label on purpose: only for name_column catalog_collections.name, with a one-line reason (linda 2026-11-22)
#   parse-removed  refused here: the Java census has no parse column (a Java name parse is P3.5a's)
# A NULL id is no collection: an id or both reader never falls back to a '' name (linda 2026-11-20).
# The two upserts (PgVectorRepository chunks, TaxonomyCentroidRepository taxonomy_centroids, op on_conflict) take the id key as their conflict target from gate 3: disposition id.
